claims.claim: Worst scenario-conditioned width, actual unknown-scenario union width and pre-outcome worst union width are three different objectives. The last admits an exact four-endpoint-pair formula.
claims.section: Unknown continuation scenarios change the audit objective
claims.scope: Fixed audited utilities, remaining utilities in [0,1], and lambda in [0,1]. No assumption that this restricted class contains real future paths. A two-state analytic example has conditioned width zero and union width 1/2.

claims.claim: With zero-sum L1 perturbation at most epsilon and two freely valued fresh coordinates, conditioned width, panel union width and pre-outcome union objective each increase by exactly epsilon. Uniform eta inflation cannot alter candidate ranking.
claims.section: Uniform ambiguity inflation is not a selector repair
claims.scope: Fresh-state utilities may attain zero and one; tube is not intersected with a tighter physically attainable continuation set. Positive/negative masses epsilon/2 are essential. Not a confidence guarantee under unspecified support restrictions.

claims.claim: At eta 0,1/8,1/4,1/2,3/4,1 the inflated model includes the final coefficient in 4,8,10,13,13,13 of the same 13 dependent nonterminal views.
claims.section: Retrospective inclusion does not establish predictive calibration
claims.scope: All views are exposed authored development paths. No statistical coverage, generalization, data-selected deployable eta or independent validation sample.

claims.claim: Both new union selectors tie their respective restricted selectors in all 16 final-width contracts. Four paired areas improve by exactly 1/192 with unchanged quote counts and query checkpoints; no new unaffected sign certificate.
claims.section: Union-aware selection changes a few states but not final identification
claims.scope: Four differences are B8/q2 one and set, B8/q3 one, B8/q4 one. They are dependent replay contrasts, not independent gains or prospective latency savings. The other 12 areas tie.

claims.claim: All 1620 actual fixed-panel decision views have scenario-union width equal to worst scenario-conditioned width, despite counterfactual pre-outcome premiums and an analytic separating example.
claims.section: Observed panel equality limits the empirical separation claim
claims.scope: Policies, caps, checkpoints and three reused panels do not create 1620 independent units. Do not describe the theoretical separation as an observed positive premium in these panels.

claims.claim: At B8/q3 late retains final safe width 1/24 and area 75/64; FIFO, restricted-set and both union rules attain width 1/12 and area 37/32. A two-quote current-disagreement rule remains nondominated on the declared width/area/quote axes despite worse width.
claims.section: A finite policy-family frontier preserves timing tradeoffs
claims.scope: Only nine predeclared rules on exposed replay. Quotes are old saved-value inspections. No globally optimal causal policy or real audit-speed frontier.

claims.claim: 173 input hashes, 540 decisions and 1620 safe-bound cells were checked; 56 original v17 terminal contracts and 420 decisions reproduce. New actual audits, natural histories, independent units and model calls remain zero.
claims.scope: Same-author verifiers use distinct formulas and enumerations, not external scientific peer review. Native Codex authoring usage is not measured.

claims.claim: An audited-set dynamic program computes the complete 2D terminal-safe-width/checkpoint-area frontier under the fixed arrival/quote contract; separate exhaustive enumeration agrees in all eight settings.
claims.scope: Fixed recovery, one instantaneous unique visible identity quote per positive integer slot, at most q. Future structure is privileged; no global online optimality.

claims.claim: All eight frontiers are singleton objective points. Of 72 preserved causal-policy rows, 28 match and 44 are dominated. The 33,658 schedule-contract combinations include nested-cap repeats.
claims.scope: Exposed twelve-template authored streams only; singleton behavior and counts are not a general scheduling theorem or independent sample denominator.

claims.claim: At B8/q3 the structural point (1/24,73/64) dominates FIFO/union (1/12,37/32) and late-prefix (1/24,75/64). At B8/q4 the point is (0,217/192), reached by none of the nine rules.
claims.scope: Legal offline witnesses read future arrivals/occupations. No proof that these headroom gaps are predictable or achievable by an online policy on new streams.

claims.claim: Three primary trajectory/debugging resources were inspected and bounded passages preserved. Attribution annotations, rerun infrastructure and deterministic complete-state recovery certification are different contracts.
claims.section: S19. Primary trajectory resources and an unclosed transfer gate
claims.scope: Read-only primary-paper/repository/card review. No data acquisition, native run, complete checkpoint proof, inherited-data license certification or external effect-size comparison.
